They even have the opportunity to redo the experiment as many times as they want without the extra need of preparation and cleaning and safety protocols that comes with doing experiments in real life.

I think the most useful aspects were the weekly lectures and quizzes, as they were a good way to cover relevant information regarding the process of addressing unmet needs, when it comes to the development, regulatory, and business sides. I also think the virtual platform was useful in order to better experience operations and other things in a better way than just watching a Youtube video.

I think for the virtual platform, the videos could be in better resolution as it is a little difficult to make out some of the finer details in these operations. Also, for the innovation notebook, I think it would be good to have deadlines for notebook entries, as otherwise I didn't really work on the innovation notebook for a while and put it on the back burner compared to other classwork and other classes.

The main thing is making the videos more higher resolution, as for some videos it was difficult to make out finer details, and it was a little blurry. Also, the videos should fully unload after you are done with them, not stay up because then it is difficult to go back and watch that video again and it just looks awkward.

I believe that the final report was the perfect final assignment for a class like this since it was actually quite enjoyable to research about the FDA regulations involved with our proposed device and the pathway we would need to take to make it happen. As a prerequisite for the BME180, this course I believe helped me a lot especially with the online lecture format due to the third-year coursework being extremely time-consuming such that I can take time out of my weekend to finally process these lectures.

There is nothing inherently wrong about the course, but something to note is that before heading into BME180, I think it would be amazing if there was a reference sheet of the business values, FDA resources, unmet needs websites like Gfinder, and other notable resources that would be worthy to add in since as soon to be graduating class of 2026, we will never gain access to this again to reference. Rather it be about theory, these resources are actually useful when bringing into BME180 where we take an idea and turn it into reality and with the proper knowledge from this class, we know what to look for in industry and faculty partners to guide us in addition to FDA checkpoints.
